title: Tomato Soup
subtitle: Classic smooth tomato soup
excerpt: A rich, smooth tomato soup made from roasted tomatoes, onion, and garlic blended with stock. Much better than tinned, and very simple once the tomatoes are roasted.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tomato soup has been a staple of British home cooking since the early twentieth century. Roasting the tomatoes rather than simmering them raw was a technique popularised by British cookery writers including Delia Smith and Nigel Slater from the 1990s onward.

recipeTools.notes: Large enough for the tomatoes in a single layer.

content.text: Tomato soup is best made by roasting the tomatoes first, which concentrates their flavour and sweetens them. After roasting, everything is blended together with stock. The result is a deep, rich soup with a natural sweetness that is completely different from anything in a tin.

Heat the oven to 200 C / fan 180 C / gas 6. Arrange the tomatoes cut-side up in a large roasting tin with the onion and garlic. Drizzle with olive oil, scatter over the salt and sugar, and tuck in the thyme. Roast for 40 minutes until the tomatoes are very soft and slightly charred at the edges.
Squeeze the garlic from its skin into a large saucepan. Add the roasted tomatoes, onion, all the roasting juices, the stock, tomato puree, and basil. Bring to a simmer.
Blend smooth with a stick blender. Pass through a sieve if you want a very smooth texture, pushing it through with a spoon.
Taste for salt, acid, and sweetness. Add a little more sugar if the tomatoes were not very ripe. Ladle into bowls and swirl over cream if using.
